notes: Help page gives no model (only a stripplot of log(total.fruits+1)). RULE GAP: model rendered from Banta et al. 2010 / Bolker et al. 2009 design (clipping x nutrient fixed; population and genotype random; rack and germination status nuisance) with random intercepts only; reg ignored because popu is nested in it (popu codes carry the region).
Help page describes the design (6 batches, 5 preparations each) but fits no model; documented model is the intercept-only batch model of the lme4 book (Bates 2010) fitted to this dataset.

Help page names a partially nested mixed model but gives no formula (examples only str/xtabs); rendered from the lme4 book / vignette model with student and lecturer crossed intercepts and service x dept fixed. RULE GAP: y is a numeric 1:5 rating, not a documented ordered factor, so response_type is continuous by the rule.
Help examples fm2; equivalent to (1|batch) + (1|sample). sample is the batch:cask combination, so ignored; cask codes a-c repeat across batches and are listed as the inner column.
Help examples fm1: crossed plate and sample random intercepts.

Help example fmVA (De Boeck and Wilson 2004). resp (ordered no<perhaps<yes) is the alternate three-level response of which r2 is the dichotomy, so ignored; mode is documented but not in the model and stays an unused column.
Help example fm1 (REML=FALSE); temp is the numeric copy of temperature, ignored. Pilot re-filing: grouping factor recipe:replicate built by the merge from its parts.
Help example m1 (binomial glmer). The observation-level model m2 adds (1|obs) with obs created in the example, not a table column, so not filed as a second model.

Help example gm1 (weights = size, binomial); equivalent to cbind(incidence, size - incidence) response. Extended version of cbpp from Lesnoff et al. 2004 with different values, so filed as its own dataset.

Help example cul_mod (binomial glmer, McKeon et al. 2012). ttt, ttt.1, crab2 and shrimp2 are relabellings of ttt2 or of crab and shrimp, ignored. RULE GAP: crab and shrimp are the factorial decomposition of ttt2, redundant with it but not a pure relabel, left as unused columns.

Help example cvm1 (tvol = log(predvolume), created in the example). RULE GAP: the fitted response is a transform of the column predvolume; the column is filed as response. The propeaten model (predvolume/volume) is not filed, its response being a ratio of two columns.
Help example cvm3 (tvol = log(predvolume)), two-way factorial version of model 1; ttt and ttt2 are the combined treatment code, ignored here.

Help example gopher_glmer (Poisson, Ozgul et al. 2009). RULE GAP: Area enters only as a log offset but is listed under covariates since it is a model column; year is a factor in the formula (3 integer values, read as categorical by the merge rule). Thin page; 30 rows, 10 sites.

Help example full_mod1 (Poisson glmer, Elston et al. 2001). RULE GAP: INDEX is the observation-level random effect (one row per level), which the merge refuses as a grouping factor, so it stays in the formula but is listed under ignore (row id) and not under grouping_factors; cHEIGHT is the centred HEIGHT, ignored.

Help example sal_mod (McCullagh and Nelder 1989, section 14.5.3). TypeM and TypeF are the two components of Cross, ignored. RULE GAP: Male and Female ids may repeat across Season/Experiment (three experiments), in which case the true groups are id by experiment; the page and example treat the ids as the groups.

Help example schmod (Gamma family, log link). imps79b and imps79o are binary and ordinal versions of the response, int is a column of ones and SqrtWeek and TxSWeek are derived; all ignored. imps79 is a 1-7 score with half-steps, so continuous.
Help example fm1 fits it with subset=Days>=2; the subset is not applied by the survey, which uses the full table.
Help example toemod (binomial glmer; de Boeck et al. 1998 trial copied from HSAUR3). visit is the sequential index of the same repeated measure as time, ignored.
